page: Vultr voc-s-32c-256gb-5760s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server configured with an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a local 5760 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this server configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance characteristics across multiple vectors. In stress-ng testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance rank in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with large-block read-only and write operations placing in the top 10% tier at 515.15 GB/sec and 253.87 GB/sec respectively. Passmark CPU evaluations, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests, consistently place in the top 25%. Database operations and static web serving throughput register in the middle 50%, while Redis SET operations demonstrate strong performance with 70.76 million operations per second.

The shared CPU allocation presents a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, uninterrupted CPU utilization, as resource contention may occur. However, the high density of memory and local NVMe storage relative to the CPU allocation provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads without the premium of dedicated CPU instances. This configuration is well-suited for large-scale database hosting, multi-threaded data decompression, memory-cached web serving, and medium-scale language model inference tasks.
